title: True or False: The Definition of Done ensures that each Increment meets the agreed quality standards before it is considered complete. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Done establishes the shared quality standards for each Increment, ensuring all completed work meets the agreed criteria. The Definition of Done helps Scrum Teams improve quality by clarifying what’s needed for each Increment. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Correct: The Definition of Done sets the minimum quality criteria that each Increment must meet to be considered complete.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is specifically designed to define the criteria for completed work and ensure quality standards are met.

title: True or False: The Definition of Done is used to create transparency by providing a shared understanding of what it means for work to be complete. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Definition of Done provides a clear standard for what it means for work to be complete, creating transparency and ensuring consistent quality. The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Correct: The Definition of Done ensures everyone understands when work is considered complete, enhancing transparency.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is specifically designed to create a shared understanding of completeness and quality.

title: Which three practices can help a Scrum Team manage technical debt without compromising Sprint Goals? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Including technical debt in the Definition of Done, dedicating part of each Sprint to address it, and using automation are key practices for managing technical debt effectively. Technical debt management ensures sustainable product quality. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Focusing solely on new features and ignoring technical debt until the product is stable.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring technical debt increases long-term risks and reduces product quality.
answer2: Including technical debt resolution as part of the Definition of Done.
explanation2: Correct: Incorporating technical debt into the Definition of Done ensures it is addressed continuously.
answer3: Allocating a percentage of each Sprint specifically for managing technical debt.
explanation3: Correct: Dedicating part of the Sprint to address technical debt helps maintain a balance between new development and quality maintenance.
answer4: Postponing all technical debt tasks to dedicated maintenance Sprints.
explanation4: Incorrect: Postponing technical debt creates a backlog of issues that can become unmanageable.
answer5: Using automated tools to identify and resolve technical debt continuously.
explanation5: Correct: Automation helps the team manage technical debt efficiently without disrupting their focus on the Sprint Goal.

title: Which two roles collaborate most closely to ensure that the Definition of Done is consistently applied to all Increments? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Developers are directly responsible for meeting the Definition of Done, with support from the Scrum Master to ensure quality standards are upheld. The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing a shared understanding of what work was completed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Product Owner and Developers
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Owner is involved in backlog management but does not directly enforce the Definition of Done.
answer2: Developers and Scrum Master
explanation2: Correct: The Developers ensure their work meets the Definition of Done, with the Scrum Master supporting by facilitating adherence to quality standards.
answer3: Scrum Master and Product Owner
explanation3: Incorrect: While the Scrum Master supports process adherence, the Product Owner is not responsible for applying the Definition of Done.
answer4: Developers and Stakeholders
explanation4: Incorrect: Stakeholders provide feedback but do not enforce the Definition of Done.
answer5: Scrum Master and Stakeholders
explanation5: Incorrect: Stakeholders are involved in feedback but not in maintaining the Definition of Done.

title: A Scrum Team is facing frequent last-minute changes from the Product Owner during the Sprint. What is the best action for the Scrum Master? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to emphasize the importance of managing changes through the Product Backlog, maintaining Sprint focus. Scrum Teams only commit to work selected during Sprint Planning. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Allow the changes to keep the Product Owner satisfied and adaptable.
explanation1: Incorrect: Allowing frequent changes disrupts the team's focus and compromises the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion with the Product Owner on the importance of maintaining the Sprint Backlog integrity and managing changes through the Product Backlog.
explanation2: Correct: Managing changes through the Product Backlog maintains Sprint focus while accommodating evolving needs.
answer3: Ignore the changes to avoid conflict with the Product Owner.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring changes can lead to misalignment and unresolved issues.
answer4: Ask the Developers to manage the changes directly with the Product Owner.
explanation4: Incorrect: Changes should be managed collectively, ensuring alignment with the Sprint Goal and Scrum processes.

title: Which two strategies can help the Scrum Master support the team in enhancing their communication and collaboration skills? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Team-building exercises and communication workshops help enhance the Scrum Team’s ability to work together effectively, fostering a collaborative environment. Effective communication is critical to a Scrum Team’s success. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Conducting one-on-one sessions to coach individual team members privately.
explanation1: Incorrect: While coaching can be valuable, collective improvement in communication is best fostered through team-wide practices.
answer2: Using team-building exercises during Retrospectives to strengthen relationships.
explanation2: Correct: Team-building activities can improve trust and communication among team members.
answer3: Encouraging the team to avoid conflicts by limiting direct communication when disagreements arise.
explanation3: Incorrect: Avoiding communication hinders collaboration and problem-solving.
answer4: Facilitating workshops on effective communication techniques tailored to the team’s needs.
explanation4: Correct: Workshops can provide practical tools and strategies to improve how the team communicates and collaborates.
answer5: Assigning the most experienced Developer to lead all discussions.
explanation5: Incorrect: Assigning a leader undermines team autonomy and balanced participation.

title: During Sprint Planning, the team disagrees on the priority of a Product Backlog item. How should the Scrum Master handle this? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to help the team align on priorities, ensuring collaborative decision-making during Sprint Planning. Sprint Planning defines what can be delivered in the Sprint and how that work will be achieved. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Decide the priority to keep the planning session moving smoothly.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not make decisions on backlog priorities.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion to ensure all perspectives are heard and guide the team toward a consensus.
explanation2: Correct: Facilitating discussions helps the team align on priorities and make collaborative decisions.
answer3: Ask the Product Owner to set the priority without team input.
explanation3: Incorrect: While the Product Owner owns backlog prioritization, team input is essential for alignment.
answer4: Move the item to the next Sprint to avoid immediate conflict.
explanation4: Incorrect: Postponing decisions disrupts planning and may impact the Sprint’s effectiveness.

title: During the Sprint, a Developer suggests a new tool that could automate part of the testing process, but it would require time to implement. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions during the Retrospective to assess new tools, ensuring changes are well-considered and aligned with team goals. The Sprint Retrospective is an opportunity to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Encourage the team to implement the tool immediately to improve efficiency.
explanation1: Incorrect: Introducing new tools mid-Sprint can disrupt focus and the planned work.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion during the next Sprint Retrospective to evaluate the potential benefits and feasibility of the tool.
explanation2: Correct: The Retrospective is a suitable event to discuss process improvements and potential tool integrations.
answer3: Reject the idea to avoid any disruptions to the current Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Improvements and innovations should be considered, but at the right time.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to decide whether the tool should be implemented.
explanation4: Incorrect: Decisions about process improvements are within the team’s remit, not the Product Owner’s responsibility.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers want to take on more work than they have capacity for. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to help the team assess their capacity and make realistic commitments during Sprint Planning, ensuring sustainable pace and focus on the Sprint Goal. The Developers can select whatever structure and techniques they want, as long as their Daily Scrum focuses on progress toward the Sprint Goal. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Encourage the Developers to take on as much work as possible to maximize productivity.
explanation1: Incorrect: Overcommitting can lead to incomplete work and burnout.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion on realistic capacity and the importance of meeting the Sprint Goal without overloading the team.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps ensure the team plans work that is achievable within their capacity.
answer3: Let the Product Owner decide how much work should be included in the Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner prioritizes the Product Backlog but does not dictate the amount of work Developers take on.
answer4: Ignore the issue as it’s up to the Developers to manage their workload.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should support the team in planning realistic workloads that align with their capacity.

title: A Scrum Team is frequently missing their Definition of Done, leading to quality issues. What is the best action for the Scrum Master? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to integrate quality practices throughout the development process, helping the team consistently meet the Definition of Done. The Definition of Done helps ensure quality standards are met consistently. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Extend the Sprint to allow the team more time to meet the Definition of Done.
explanation1: Incorrect: Extending the Sprint disrupts the Scrum cadence and is not allowed.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion on how the team can integrate quality practices earlier in the development process to meet the Definition of Done consistently.
explanation2: Correct: Integrating quality practices helps the team meet standards consistently and improve their delivery.
answer3: Assign specific Developers to handle quality checks before work is considered done.
explanation3: Incorrect: Quality is a collective responsibility, not the task of individual Developers.
answer4: Ignore the issue as it’s normal for some items to miss the Definition of Done.
explanation4: Incorrect: Consistently missing the Definition of Done indicates a need for process improvement.

title: Which two approaches can help a Scrum Team avoid common pitfalls during Product Backlog refinement? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: Regular refinement sessions and open communication between the Product Owner and Developers help maintain a clear, actionable Product Backlog, avoiding common pitfalls. Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ensuring only the Product Owner refines the backlog to maintain control over priorities.
explanation1: Incorrect: Refinement should be a collaborative effort between the Product Owner and Developers.
answer2: Encouraging open communication between Developers and the Product Owner to clarify items and prioritize effectively.
explanation2: Correct: Collaboration during refinement ensures clarity and alignment on priorities.
answer3: Setting aside regular time each Sprint for refinement sessions to keep the backlog manageable.
explanation3: Correct: Regular refinement sessions help keep the Product Backlog clear, actionable, and prioritized.
answer4: Assigning refinement to a dedicated team member to ensure consistency.
explanation4: Incorrect: Refinement is a shared responsibility and should not be delegated to one person.
answer5: Skipping refinement sessions if the team feels the backlog is already clear.
explanation5: Incorrect: Regular refinement helps maintain the quality and clarity of backlog items.

title: Which three practices help mitigate the impact of common anti-patterns in Daily Scrums? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Maintaining focus on the Sprint Goal, keeping discussions concise, and addressing impediments promptly help the team manage common Daily Scrum anti-patterns effectively. The Daily Scrum improves communication, identifies impediments, and promotes quick decision-making. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Encouraging each team member to give detailed status reports.
explanation1: Incorrect: Status reporting is not the purpose of the Daily Scrum; it focuses on planning for the next 24 hours.
answer2: Focusing on progress toward the Sprint Goal.
explanation2: Correct: Focusing on the Sprint Goal aligns the team on what’s important, reducing the impact of side issues.
answer3: Limiting discussions to what’s essential for the team’s planning.
explanation3: Correct: Keeping the conversation focused helps maintain the efficiency and purpose of the Daily Scrum.
answer4: Involving stakeholders in Daily Scrums for additional perspectives.
explanation4: Incorrect: Daily Scrums are for Developers, not stakeholders; their participation can distract from the team’s focus.
answer5: Encouraging team members to raise impediments as they occur.
explanation5: Correct: Promptly addressing impediments helps keep the team on track and mitigates process disruptions.

title: A Scrum Team is struggling to maintain consistent velocity due to external dependencies. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to help the team manage and mitigate dependencies, ensuring consistent planning and delivery. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team remove impediments to the team’s progress. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Escalate the issue to management and request more resources to manage dependencies.
explanation1: Incorrect: Escalation should be a last resort; the team should first seek to resolve the dependencies internally.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion with the team to identify ways to manage or mitigate dependencies, possibly incorporating these strategies into their planning.
explanation2: Correct: Addressing dependencies collaboratively helps the team find ways to manage them effectively within their control.
answer3: Ignore the dependencies and focus solely on the work within the team's control.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring dependencies can lead to incomplete work and inconsistent velocity.
answer4: Assign specific team members to manage the dependencies separately.
explanation4: Incorrect: Managing dependencies should be a collective effort, not assigned to specific individuals.

title: Which three strategies can help a Scrum Team integrate stakeholder feedback more effectively into their process? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Using Sprint Reviews, involving stakeholders in refinement, and maintaining feedback loops are effective strategies for integrating stakeholder input into the Scrum process. Stakeholder collaboration is key to aligning the product with market needs. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Scheduling additional meetings outside of official Scrum events to gather feedback.
explanation1: Incorrect: Feedback should be integrated through established Scrum events like Sprint Reviews and backlog refinement.
answer2: Using the Sprint Review as a primary forum for gathering stakeholder feedback on the Increment.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Review is specifically designed to engage stakeholders and adapt the Product Backlog accordingly.
answer3: Involving stakeholders in Product Backlog refinement to align on priorities and expectations.
explanation3: Correct: Stakeholder involvement in refinement helps ensure that the Product Backlog reflects current needs and priorities.
answer4: Documenting all feedback and assigning action items to specific team members.
explanation4: Incorrect: Feedback should inform backlog updates, not be treated as individual action items for immediate execution.
answer5: Regularly updating stakeholders on how their feedback has been incorporated into the product.
explanation5: Correct: Providing feedback loops to stakeholders helps maintain engagement and ensures their input is valued and utilized.

title: Which three actions can a Scrum Team take to ensure their Definition of Done remains relevant and effective? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Regular reviews, aligning with industry standards, and incorporating stakeholder feedback help ensure the Definition of Done remains relevant and effective. The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing a shared understanding of what work was completed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Reviewing the Definition of Done during each Sprint Retrospective to adjust as necessary.
explanation1: Correct: Regular reviews during Retrospectives help the team refine their standards to meet evolving needs.
answer2: Only changing the Definition of Done when issues are identified during development.
explanation2: Incorrect: Proactive reviews, not just reactive changes, keep the Definition of Done relevant.
answer3: Including quality metrics that align with industry standards in the Definition of Done.
explanation3: Correct: Aligning the Definition of Done with industry standards helps ensure that quality remains consistent and competitive.
answer4: Setting the Definition of Done once at the start of the project and not revisiting it.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done should evolve with the team’s growing understanding and capabilities.
answer5: Incorporating feedback from stakeholders into the Definition of Done to reflect external quality expectations.
explanation5: Correct: Stakeholder input helps ensure that the Definition of Done meets both internal and external quality expectations.

title: Which three pillars of Scrum support the implementation of empirical process control? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Transparency, Inspection, and Adaptation are the three pillars of Scrum that support empirical process control, allowing the team to continuously improve their work process. These pillars are critical to Scrum’s success. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Transparency
explanation1: Correct: Transparency ensures that the process and work are visible to those responsible for the outcome, enabling inspection and adaptation.
answer2: Accountability
explanation2: Incorrect: Accountability is important but not one of the three pillars of Scrum.
answer3: Inspection
explanation3: Correct: Inspection allows the team to regularly check their progress and adjust their course of action if necessary.
answer4: Adaptation
explanation4: Correct: Adaptation enables the team to make adjustments based on the results of inspection to optimize outcomes.
answer5: Commitment
explanation5: Incorrect: Commitment is a value, not one of the pillars of Scrum.

title: Which two factors are critical in creating a clear and effective Definition of Done? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Definition of Done should align with organizational standards and be agreed upon by the entire Scrum Team to ensure high quality and consistency. The Definition of Done is a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets the quality measures required for the product. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Alignment with organizational standards and policies.
explanation1: Correct: A good Definition of Done aligns with broader organizational quality standards.
answer2: Frequent changes to adapt to team preferences.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Definition of Done should remain stable to maintain consistency.
answer3: Agreement among the entire Scrum Team on what constitutes completion.
explanation3: Correct: The Scrum Team must agree on the Definition of Done to ensure consistency in the quality of work.
answer4: Set by the Product Owner alone to control quality.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is a collaborative standard, not dictated by one role.
answer5: Changing with every Sprint to fit new goals.
explanation5: Incorrect: Stability in the Definition of Done is crucial for maintaining product quality.

title: Which actions should a Scrum Master take if a Scrum Team is struggling to meet their Definition of Done consistently? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions during the Retrospective and coach the team on improving their practices to consistently meet the Definition of Done. The Definition of Done creates transparency by providing everyone a shared understanding of what work was completed as part of the Increment. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Facilitate a discussion during the Retrospective to explore causes and solutions.
explanation1: Correct: The Retrospective is an opportunity to inspect challenges and plan for improvements.
answer2: Lower the standards of the Definition of Done to make it more achievable.
explanation2: Incorrect: Lowering quality standards undermines the team’s commitment to delivering high-value work.
answer3: Coach the team on techniques to improve quality and meet the Definition of Done.
explanation3: Correct: Coaching can help the team develop better practices to meet their quality standards.
answer4: Allow the Product Owner to redefine what Done means.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is defined by the whole team, not just the Product Owner.
answer5: Ignore the issue if it does not impact the current Sprint.
explanation5: Incorrect: Consistently meeting the Definition of Done is critical to delivering high-quality Increments.

title: A Scrum Team consistently fails to complete work committed during the Sprint Planning. What should the team do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Developers should adapt their planning to commit to a more realistic workload based on their capacity, improving predictability. The Developers forecast the work that can be accomplished during the Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Commit to less work in the next Sprint Planning.
explanation1: Correct: The team should adjust their commitment to match their capacity, ensuring more realistic planning.
answer2: Continue committing the same amount of work and push harder.
explanation2: Incorrect: Overcommitting can lead to burnout and decreased performance.
answer3: Ask the Product Owner to help prioritize work during the Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Prioritization is set during Sprint Planning and is not adjusted mid-Sprint.
answer4: Add more team members to increase capacity.
explanation4: Incorrect: Adding members is not an immediate solution and requires consideration of team dynamics.

title: A Scrum Team has identified a recurring issue with their Definition of Done not being met. What should the Scrum Master do to help the team improve? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate workshops to help the team review and adjust their Definition of Done, ensuring it is achievable and supports consistent quality standards. The Definition of Done helps create a shared understanding of what is considered complete. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Reduce the criteria in the Definition of Done to make it easier to meet.
explanation1: Incorrect: Reducing criteria compromises quality and does not address the root cause of recurring issues.
answer2: Facilitate a workshop to review and adjust the Definition of Done, ensuring it is clear, achievable, and aligned with team capabilities.
explanation2: Correct: Reviewing and adjusting the Definition of Done helps the team set realistic standards that maintain quality.
answer3: Assign specific team members to focus solely on meeting the Definition of Done for each Increment.
explanation3: Incorrect: Meeting the Definition of Done is a shared responsibility, not assigned to individuals.
answer4: Ignore the issue as long as most of the work meets the expected quality standards.
explanation4: Incorrect: Ignoring issues with the Definition of Done can lead to inconsistent quality and stakeholder dissatisfaction.

title: A Scrum Team often rushes to complete their Definition of Done criteria at the end of each Sprint. What is the best course of action for the Scrum Master? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate workshops to help the team integrate Definition of Done criteria throughout the development process, ensuring continuous quality assurance. The Definition of Done helps create a shared understanding of what is considered complete. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ask the team to lower the Definition of Done criteria to make it easier to achieve.
explanation1: Incorrect: Lowering quality standards compromises the product’s value and integrity.
answer2: Facilitate workshops on integrating Definition of Done criteria throughout the development process, ensuring quality checks are continuous.
explanation2: Correct: Integrating quality checks early helps the team meet the Definition of Done consistently and sustainably.
answer3: Assign quality assurance tasks to specific team members to handle towards the end of each Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Quality is a shared responsibility and should be integrated throughout the development process.
answer4: Ignore the issue, trusting the team will eventually improve on their own.
explanation4: Incorrect: Proactive facilitation helps the team embed quality practices and avoid last-minute rushes.

title: During the Sprint, the Developers realize they will not meet the Definition of Done for a key item. What should they do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Developers should use the Daily Scrum to inspect and adapt their work plan, ensuring that all items meet the Definition of Done by the end of the Sprint. The Developers create a plan for the Sprint, the Sprint Backlog, and adapt their plan each day toward the Sprint Goal. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Mark the item as complete and address the missing parts in the next Sprint.
explanation1: Incorrect: Incomplete work should not be considered done; it must meet the Definition of Done to be counted as complete.
answer2: Communicate the issue during the Daily Scrum and adjust their plan to meet the Definition of Done.
explanation2: Correct: The team should adapt their plan to ensure that work meets the Definition of Done within the Sprint.
answer3: Ask the Product Owner to lower the Definition of Done standards temporarily.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Definition of Done should remain consistent and not be altered for convenience.
answer4: Ignore the issue and continue working on other tasks.
explanation4: Incorrect: Ignoring quality issues compromises the Increment’s value and quality.

title: The Scrum Master notices that the team frequently struggles with the Definition of Done. What should they do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to help the team improve their Definition of Done, ensuring they consistently meet the standards required for the Increment. The Definition of Done is a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets the quality measures required for the product. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Lower the Definition of Done standards to make them easier to achieve.
explanation1: Incorrect: Lowering standards undermines the quality and value of the Increment.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion to improve the Definition of Done and help the team meet it consistently.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should facilitate improvements to ensure the team meets the Definition of Done consistently.
answer3: Ignore the issue and focus on completing work faster.
explanation3: Incorrect: Ignoring quality issues does not align with Scrum principles of delivering high-value Increments.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to redefine the Definition of Done.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is created by the entire Scrum Team, not just the Product Owner.

title: What is the best way to handle non-functional requirements in Scrum? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Non-functional requirements are handled by incorporating them into the Product Backlog, ensuring they are prioritized and visible along with all other work. Product Backlog items that can be done by the Developers within one Sprint are deemed ready for selection in Sprint Planning. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Integrate them into the Product Backlog and prioritize with other items.
explanation1: Correct: Non-functional requirements should be visible and managed like any other work.
answer2: Handle them during a separate Sprint.
explanation2: Incorrect: Scrum does not support special Sprints for specific types of work.
answer3: Address them only when they cause issues in the product.
explanation3: Incorrect: Non-functional requirements should be proactively managed, not only when problems arise.
answer4: Assign them to a specialist outside of the team.
explanation4: Incorrect: The entire Scrum Team should work on all aspects of the product, including non-functional requirements.

title: Which Scrum value is demonstrated when the team collaborates openly to resolve issues? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Openness is a core Scrum value that fosters an environment where team members freely share information and collaborate effectively to address challenges. The Scrum Team and its stakeholders agree to be open about all the work and the challenges with performing the work. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Focus
explanation1: Incorrect: Focus involves concentrating on the Sprint Goal but does not specifically relate to collaboration.
answer2: Openness
explanation2: Correct: Openness encourages team members to be transparent, share information, and work together to solve problems.
answer3: Courage
explanation3: Incorrect: Courage involves taking risks and facing challenges but does not directly relate to collaboration.
answer4: Respect
explanation4: Incorrect: Respect involves valuing others’ contributions but is not specifically about collaboration.

title: True or False: The Product Owner is responsible for maximizing the value of the product by managing the Product Backlog. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product through careful management of the Product Backlog. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner maximizes product value through effective Product Backlog management.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner’s main role is to maximize value by managing the Product Backlog effectively.

title: True or False: The Product Owner is responsible for maximizing the value of the product by managing the Product Backlog. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Owner manages the Product Backlog to maximize the value delivered by the Scrum Team’s work. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Correct: The Product Owner prioritizes and manages the Product Backlog to maximize product value.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner is solely responsible for maximizing product value through backlog management.

title: A Product Owner often assigns tasks directly to Developers during the Sprint, disrupting their planned work. How should this be handled? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate understanding of the roles, reminding the Product Owner to focus on priorities and letting the Developers manage their own work. The Scrum Master serves the Product Owner by helping to find techniques for effective Product Backlog management. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Remind the Product Owner that the team self-organizes to manage their work.
explanation1: Correct: Developers are responsible for managing their work, and the Product Owner should respect this autonomy.
answer2: Include the Product Owner in Daily Scrums to keep them informed.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Owner’s attendance is optional and does not address the issue of task assignment.
answer3: Facilitate a discussion about roles and responsibilities in Scrum.
explanation3: Correct: A clear understanding of each role can help prevent misunderstandings and overreach.
answer4: Encourage the Product Owner to focus on setting priorities, not assigning tasks.
explanation4: Correct: The Product Owner sets priorities in the Product Backlog but should not assign tasks directly.
answer5: Allow the Developers to push back on the assignments independently.
explanation5: Incorrect: While self-management is important, facilitating clear roles helps avoid conflict.

title: What are the key responsibilities of the Scrum Master in ensuring the Scrum Team's effectiveness? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master facilitates Scrum events and removes impediments to help the team stay effective and focused on delivering value. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team improve its practices, within the Scrum framework. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Assign tasks to Developers to optimize productivity.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master does not assign tasks; the team is self-managing.
answer2: Facilitate Scrum events to ensure they are productive and focused.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master facilitates events, ensuring they meet their intended outcomes.
answer3: Remove impediments that are hindering the team’s progress.
explanation3: Correct: Removing impediments is a core responsibility of the Scrum Master to help the team remain effective.
answer4: Report team performance metrics to stakeholders.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master focuses on the team’s process, not on reporting performance metrics.
answer5: Take over Product Owner responsibilities if they are absent.
explanation5: Incorrect: The roles in Scrum are distinct and should not be combined or taken over.

title: Which two actions can the Scrum Master take if a team member frequently misses Daily Scrums? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master can support the team by encouraging participation and facilitating discussions that emphasize the value of the Daily Scrum. The Scrum Master helps everyone understand Scrum theory and practice. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Remind the team member of their commitment to the team.
explanation1: Correct: Reminding them of their commitment helps reinforce the importance of participation.
answer2: Exclude the member from future Daily Scrums until attendance improves.
explanation2: Incorrect: Exclusion contradicts the collaborative nature of Scrum.
answer3: Facilitate a team discussion on the importance of Daily Scrums.
explanation3: Correct: Facilitating discussions encourages the team to reflect on and improve their practices.
answer4: Report the behavior to management for disciplinary action.
explanation4: Incorrect: Management intervention is not aligned with Scrum principles.
answer5: Ignore the issue, as it is the team member’s choice.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should support the team in understanding the importance of participation.

title: Which two responsibilities are central to the role of the Scrum Master in supporting the Scrum Team? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master’s core responsibilities include facilitating Scrum events and helping the team remove impediments to their progress. The Scrum Master serves the Scrum Team by helping them improve their practices and effectiveness. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Assigning tasks to Developers based on their skills.
explanation1: Incorrect: The team self-organizes; the Scrum Master does not assign tasks.
answer2: Facilitating Scrum events as requested or needed.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master ensures that Scrum events are productive and effective.
answer3: Helping the team remove impediments that hinder their progress.
explanation3: Correct: The Scrum Master actively works to help the team overcome obstacles.
answer4: Reporting the team’s progress to stakeholders.
explanation4: Incorrect: Stakeholder communication is primarily managed by the Product Owner.
answer5: Creating the Definition of Done for the team.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is created collaboratively by the team.

title: Which two roles are essential in refining the Product Backlog? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner and Developers collaborate to refine the Product Backlog, ensuring items are clear, actionable, and prioritized. The Product Owner and Developers collaborate on Product Backlog refinement as needed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Scrum Master and Developers
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not directly refine the Product Backlog.
answer2: Product Owner and Developers
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner and Developers work together to refine and clarify the Product Backlog items.
answer3: Scrum Master and Product Owner
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner leads the refinement process, supported by the Developers.
answer4: Developers and Stakeholders
explanation4: Incorrect: Stakeholders provide feedback, but refinement is managed by the Product Owner and Developers.
answer5: Scrum Master and Stakeholders
explanation5: Incorrect: The Scrum Master and Stakeholders do not manage refinement directly.

title: A Developer frequently misses the Daily Scrum, impacting team collaboration. What is the best action for the Scrum Master? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should address attendance issues by facilitating a conversation with the Developer to encourage regular participation in the Daily Scrum. The Daily Scrum improves communication, identifies impediments, and promotes quick decision-making. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ignore the absences as it is the Developer’s personal choice.
explanation1: Incorrect: Regular attendance is essential for team collaboration and progress.
answer2: Facilitate a conversation with the Developer to understand the reasons for the absences and encourage participation.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master supports the team by addressing attendance issues constructively.
answer3: Require the Developer to submit a written report instead of attending the Daily Scrum.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is intended for real-time collaboration, not reporting.
answer4: Exclude the Developer from future Sprints until they commit to attending.
explanation4: Incorrect: Exclusion is not a constructive approach and could harm team dynamics.

title: A Developer is frequently taking on tasks beyond their expertise, leading to delays. How should the Scrum Master address this? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions on skill development and encourage pairing or mentoring, helping the team become more versatile and effective. The Scrum Team is cross-functional, meaning the members have all the skills necessary to create value each Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Reassign tasks to match the Developer’s skills more closely to avoid future delays.
explanation1: Incorrect: Task assignment should be managed collectively and encourage skill development, not just match current expertise.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion on skill development and encourage pairing or mentoring to build expertise within the team.
explanation2: Correct: Encouraging skill development helps the team become more cross-functional and reduces dependency on specific individuals.
answer3: Ignore the issue, assuming the Developer will eventually improve on their own.
explanation3: Incorrect: Addressing skill gaps proactively supports continuous learning and team effectiveness.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to assign simpler tasks to the Developer to avoid delays.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner prioritizes items but does not assign tasks to individual team members.

title: A Product Owner is consistently unavailable to answer questions about the Product Backlog items during the Sprint. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to ensure the Product Owner understands their role in supporting the team during the Sprint. The Product Owner is accountable for maximizing the value of the product resulting from the work of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ask the Developers to make assumptions and proceed with the work.
explanation1: Incorrect: Assumptions can lead to misalignment and errors.
answer2: Facilitate a conversation with the Product Owner to ensure they understand the importance of availability for the team.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps improve communication and ensures the Product Owner is available to support the team.
answer3: Escalate the issue to upper management to address the Product Owner’s unavailability.
explanation3: Incorrect: This issue should be resolved within the Scrum Team without external escalation.
answer4: Ignore the issue and continue working on other available tasks.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should address the issue to avoid misalignment and blockages.

title: A Scrum Team is consistently interrupted during Sprints by requests for updates from various stakeholders. How should the Scrum Master address this issue? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate the establishment of communication protocols that help the team maintain focus while ensuring stakeholders are kept informed through appropriate channels. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team focus on creating high-value Increments. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Instruct the team to ignore all external communications during the Sprint to maintain focus.
explanation1: Incorrect: Ignoring stakeholder communications can lead to misalignment and missed opportunities for feedback.
answer2: Facilitate the establishment of clear communication protocols that direct stakeholders to the Product Owner for updates.
explanation2: Correct: Setting communication protocols helps the team focus while ensuring stakeholders receive necessary updates through appropriate channels.
answer3: Encourage the team to provide frequent updates directly to stakeholders as needed.
explanation3: Incorrect: Direct updates during the Sprint can cause disruptions and reduce team productivity.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to handle all stakeholder communications independently.
explanation4: Incorrect: While the Product Owner manages stakeholder expectations, communication protocols should involve the whole team.

title: A Scrum Team is struggling with unclear requirements that frequently change. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate communication between the Developers and the Product Owner to ensure that requirements are clear and aligned. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team improve its practices within the Scrum framework. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ask the Developers to proceed with their best guess.
explanation1: Incorrect: Working on assumptions can lead to errors and inefficiencies.
answer2: Facilitate a session between the Developers and the Product Owner to clarify and refine the requirements.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master supports collaboration and clarity between the Developers and Product Owner.
answer3: Remove the unclear requirements from the Sprint Backlog.
explanation3: Incorrect: Requirements should be clarified, not removed impulsively.
answer4: Extend the Sprint to allow more time for clarification.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprints are time-boxed and should not be extended.

title: During a Sprint, a Developer is blocked by an external dependency that wasn't identified during Sprint Planning. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should help the team manage the impediment by facilitating a discussion to explore possible solutions. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team remove impediments to the team’s progress. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Instruct the Developer to wait until the dependency is resolved.
explanation1: Incorrect: Waiting without taking action can cause further delays.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion with the team to explore ways to manage or mitigate the dependency.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps the team identify and remove impediments to maintain progress.
answer3: Report the issue to management for immediate intervention.
explanation3: Incorrect: Management intervention should be a last resort; the team should try to resolve it internally.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to handle the dependency.
explanation4: Incorrect: Handling technical dependencies is primarily the responsibility of the Developers, facilitated by the Scrum Master.

title: During a Sprint, the Developers discover that they are missing a key skill needed to complete a Product Backlog item. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate skill development within the team, promoting a self-managing environment. The Scrum Master helps the Scrum Team improve their practices within the Scrum framework. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Arrange for an external consultant to help with the task.
explanation1: Incorrect: Bringing in external help undermines the self-managing nature of the team.
answer2: Facilitate learning and skill-sharing among the Developers.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should encourage the team to learn and grow by sharing skills.
answer3: Remove the item from the Sprint Backlog.
explanation3: Incorrect: Removing items disrupts the Sprint Goal and should be avoided unless critical.
answer4: Ask the Product Owner to reprioritize the work.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner manages backlog priorities, not mid-Sprint work adjustments.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers identify that an item requires external expertise that the team lacks. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions to address skill gaps, supporting the team in finding collaborative solutions to manage complex work effectively. The Scrum Team is cross-functional, meaning the members have all the skills necessary to create value each Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Assign the task to the most experienced Developer on the team regardless of expertise.
explanation1: Incorrect: Assigning tasks based on availability rather than skill can lead to suboptimal results.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion on how to address the skill gap, such as training, pairing, or temporarily bringing in outside expertise.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master supports the team in finding ways to handle skill gaps collaboratively.
answer3: Delay the work until the team acquires the necessary skills in a future Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Delaying critical work may impact the Product Goal; exploring immediate solutions is preferred.
answer4: Escalate the issue to management to provide the necessary resources.
explanation4: Incorrect: Escalation should be a last resort; the team should first attempt to find a solution internally.

title: True or False: The Product Backlog refinement is an official Scrum event with a set time box. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Product Backlog refinement is an ongoing activity that keeps the backlog manageable, without being a formal event or having a set time box. Refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Incorrect: Product Backlog refinement is an activity, not an official Scrum event, and it does not have a set time box.
explanation2: Correct: Refinement is an ongoing activity that helps keep the Product Backlog manageable and is not officially time-boxed.

title: Which three best practices can help a Scrum Team maintain a transparent and manageable Product Backlog? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Maintaining a transparent and manageable Product Backlog involves regular refinement, stakeholder feedback, and continuous updates to reflect the latest insights and priorities. Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Regular refinement sessions to clarify and prioritize items.
explanation1: Correct: Regular refinement ensures that the Product Backlog remains clear and actionable.
answer2: Detailed task lists for each Developer.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Product Backlog focuses on items and their priority, not on task lists.
answer3: Stakeholder involvement to provide feedback and adjust priorities.
explanation3: Correct: Stakeholder feedback helps keep the backlog aligned with current needs and priorities.
answer4: Continuous updates based on team feedback and completed work insights.
explanation4: Correct: Regular updates based on feedback ensure the backlog remains relevant and prioritized.
answer5: Assigning tasks directly to Developers during refinement.
explanation5: Incorrect: Refinement is about prioritizing and clarifying items, not assigning tasks.

title: Which three elements are crucial for maintaining a transparent Product Backlog? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Regular refinement, stakeholder input, and using tools that enhance visibility help maintain a transparent Product Backlog, supporting effective team alignment. The Product Backlog is an emergent, ordered list of what is needed to improve the product. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ensuring that all items are fully detailed before adding them to the Product Backlog.
explanation1: Incorrect: Over-detailing items can slow down the process and limit flexibility; clarity and actionability are key.
answer2: Regularly refining the Product Backlog to keep items up-to-date, prioritized, and actionable.
explanation2: Correct: Continuous refinement ensures the backlog reflects current priorities and supports effective Sprint Planning.
answer3: Including input from stakeholders during refinement to align the backlog with market needs and expectations.
explanation3: Correct: Stakeholder input helps ensure the backlog is aligned with evolving needs and provides maximum value.
answer4: Using backlog management tools that provide visibility into item status, priority, and dependencies.
explanation4: Correct: Tools that enhance transparency help the team manage the backlog more effectively and make informed decisions.
answer5: Relying solely on the Product Owner to manage and update the backlog independently.
explanation5: Incorrect: Product Backlog management is a collaborative effort, not the sole responsibility of the Product Owner.

title: Which three key factors contribute to a well-maintained Product Backlog? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Engaging stakeholders, refining items regularly, and using Retrospective feedback help maintain a well-aligned and actionable Product Backlog. Product Backlog refinement is the act of adding detail, estimates, and order to items in the Product Backlog. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Only updating the Product Backlog during formal Scrum events like Sprint Planning and Reviews.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog should be continuously updated as needed to reflect the latest priorities and insights.
answer2: Engaging stakeholders regularly to gather feedback and incorporate it into the backlog.
explanation2: Correct: Stakeholder feedback ensures the backlog aligns with evolving needs and expectations.
answer3: Regularly refining backlog items to add detail, estimates, and adjust priorities.
explanation3: Correct: Ongoing refinement keeps the backlog actionable and aligned with the team’s capacity.
answer4: Using feedback from the Sprint Retrospective to adjust and improve the backlog management process.
explanation4: Correct: Retrospective insights help the team refine their processes, improving backlog management over time.
answer5: Delegating backlog refinement solely to the Product Owner to maintain control.
explanation5: Incorrect: Refinement should be a collaborative process involving the whole team.

title: Which two roles are essential during the refinement of the Product Backlog to ensure items are well-prepared for future Sprints? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner and Developers work together during refinement to ensure that Product Backlog items are clear, well-understood, and ready for upcoming Sprints. Product Backlog refinement is a continuous process of keeping the backlog ordered and actionable. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Scrum Master and Stakeholders
explanation1: Incorrect: While stakeholders provide input, they do not directly manage backlog refinement.
answer2: Product Owner and Developers
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner and Developers collaborate to refine items, ensuring they are clear, actionable, and ready for future Sprints.
answer3: Scrum Master and Product Owner
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Owner leads refinement, while the Scrum Master facilitates the process but does not directly refine the backlog.
answer4: Developers and Stakeholders
explanation4: Incorrect: Stakeholders provide feedback, but refinement is managed by the Product Owner and Developers.
answer5: Scrum Master and Developers
explanation5: Incorrect: The Developers refine the backlog with the Product Owner, supported by the Scrum Master in facilitation roles.

title: Which two Scrum artifacts are most directly linked to providing transparency about the work being done during the Sprint? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog and Increment provide the most transparency about ongoing work and the results of that work during the Sprint. The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers, and the Increment is the sum of all completed work at the end of the Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog provides transparency about future work, not current Sprint work.
answer2: Sprint Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Backlog shows the work planned for the Sprint and helps track progress.
answer3: Increment
explanation3: Correct: The Increment represents the work completed during the Sprint, showing what has been achieved.
answer4: Definition of Done
explanation4: Incorrect: The Definition of Done sets quality standards but does not track ongoing work.
answer5: Burnup Chart
explanation5: Incorrect: While useful, it is not an official Scrum artifact.

title: During Product Backlog refinement, a Scrum Team is unsure how to prioritize items effectively. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate prioritization workshops to help the team and Product Owner align on priorities, ensuring that the most valuable items are addressed first. Product Backlog refinement is key to maintaining an actionable and prioritized backlog. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ask the Product Owner to decide on priorities without input from the team to speed up the process.
explanation1: Incorrect: Prioritization should be a collaborative process, reflecting both stakeholder needs and team input.
answer2: Facilitate a prioritization workshop using techniques like MoSCoW or value vs. effort analysis to help the team and Product Owner align on priorities.
explanation2: Correct: Prioritization workshops help the team and Product Owner make informed decisions based on value and effort.
answer3: Allow the team to work on items in any order they prefer, without prioritization constraints.
explanation3: Incorrect: Working without prioritization can lead to misalignment with stakeholder needs and strategic goals.
answer4: Ignore the prioritization issue, trusting the team will eventually develop a natural order of work.
explanation4: Incorrect: Structured prioritization helps ensure that the most valuable work is tackled first.

title: What is the main purpose of the Increment in Scrum? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Increment is a usable, potentially shippable product that adds value and represents completed work meeting the Definition of Done. The Increment is a concrete stepping stone toward the Product Goal. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: To demonstrate all the work completed during the project.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Increment shows the work completed during the Sprint, not the entire project.
answer2: To provide a usable and potentially shippable product that adds value to the stakeholders.
explanation2: Correct: Each Increment builds on the previous ones, providing usable value.
answer3: To track the progress of the team’s work.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment reflects completed work, not ongoing progress.
answer4: To plan the next Sprint’s tasks.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Increment is the result of completed work, not a planning tool.

title: What is the primary purpose of the Product Backlog in Scrum? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Product Backlog is a continuously updated list of all work needed for the product, ordered by priority to maximize value. The Product Backlog is an ordered list of everything that is known to be needed in the product. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: To assign work to Developers based on their expertise.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog does not assign tasks; it is a prioritized list of work needed for the product.
answer2: To provide a dynamic, prioritized list of all work needed to improve the product.
explanation2: Correct: The Product Backlog is managed by the Product Owner and continuously updated to maximize value.
answer3: To track the progress of completed tasks.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Product Backlog focuses on future work, not tracking what has been done.
answer4: To ensure all team members are equally busy.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Backlog aims to maximize product value, not to distribute workload evenly.

title: Which artifact is used to measure progress toward completing work during a Sprint? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Backlog is used by the Developers to track progress and adjust the work needed to meet the Sprint Goal. The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Product Backlog
explanation1: Incorrect: The Product Backlog is a list of all work needed for the product, not specific to the Sprint.
answer2: Sprint Backlog
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Backlog includes the planned work and helps track progress toward the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Increment
explanation3: Incorrect: The Increment is the result of completed work, not a tracker of ongoing work.
answer4: Burnup Chart
explanation4: Incorrect: Although useful, it is not a core Scrum artifact.

title: True or False: The Daily Scrum helps the team inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adjust their plan accordingly. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Daily Scrum is designed to help the team inspect their progress and make necessary adjustments to achieve the Sprint Goal. The purpose of the Daily Scrum is to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt the Sprint Backlog as necessary. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Correct: The Daily Scrum is a key event where the team inspects their progress and adapts their plan to stay on track.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum focuses specifically on inspecting progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapting as necessary.

title: True or False: The Scrum Master is responsible for assigning tasks to Developers during the Daily Scrum. (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Developers are responsible for managing their tasks; the Scrum Master facilitates the process but does not assign tasks. The Developers can select whatever structure and techniques they want, as long as their Daily Scrum focuses on progress toward the Sprint Goal. (Scrum Guide 2020)
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master does not assign tasks; the Developers self-manage their work.
explanation2: Correct: The Developers self-organize and manage their own tasks, with the Scrum Master facilitating as needed.

title: Which three elements should be included in the Sprint Planning process? (Choose the three best answers)
feedback: Sprint Planning involves defining the Sprint Goal, selecting items for the Sprint Backlog, and creating a plan to achieve the goal. Sprint Planning sets the focus and defines what can be delivered during the Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Defining the Sprint Goal.
explanation1: Correct: The Sprint Goal sets the focus and purpose of the Sprint.
answer2: Selecting items from the Product Backlog to work on.
explanation2: Correct: The team selects work items from the Product Backlog that will be included in the Sprint Backlog.
answer3: Assigning specific tasks to each Developer.
explanation3: Incorrect: Task assignment is not part of Sprint Planning; the Developers self-organize their work.
answer4: Creating a detailed task list for the Sprint.
explanation4: Correct: A plan is made on how to achieve the Sprint Goal and complete the selected Product Backlog items.
answer5: Revising the Definition of Done.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Definition of Done is not typically revised during Sprint Planning; it guides the quality of the Increment.

title: Which two actions are essential for the Scrum Master to support the Scrum Team during the Daily Scrum? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Scrum Master supports the team by encouraging open communication and ensuring the team addresses impediments during the Daily Scrum. The Daily Scrum is an internal meeting for the Developers of the Scrum Team. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Leading the Daily Scrum to ensure it stays on track.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is led by the Developers, not the Scrum Master.
answer2: Ensuring the team addresses impediments and adjusts their plan as needed.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master helps the team focus on progress toward the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Encouraging open communication and collaboration among team members.
explanation3: Correct: Open communication fosters a productive Daily Scrum environment.
answer4: Assigning tasks to team members to ensure progress.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Scrum Master does not assign tasks; the team self-organizes.
answer5: Documenting each team member’s progress for performance tracking.
explanation5: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is for the team’s use, not for documenting performance.

title: Which two roles collaborate most closely during Sprint Planning to ensure the work selected is achievable? (Choose the two best answers)
feedback: The Product Owner and Developers work closely during Sprint Planning to ensure that the selected work aligns with priorities and is achievable within the Sprint. The Developers are responsible for all estimates of work done in the Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Developers and Stakeholders
explanation1: Incorrect: Stakeholders are not directly involved in Sprint Planning; their input is considered through the Product Backlog.
answer2: Product Owner and Developers
explanation2: Correct: The Product Owner provides the prioritized items, and the Developers assess what can be accomplished.
answer3: Scrum Master and Product Owner
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates the planning process but does not directly decide on the work selected.
answer4: Developers and Scrum Master
explanation4: Incorrect: While the Scrum Master facilitates, the Developers make the final decisions on what work they can accomplish.
answer5: Product Owner and Stakeholders
explanation5: Incorrect: Stakeholders influence priorities, but they are not involved in the detailed planning of the Sprint.

title: A Scrum Team is finding it difficult to collaborate effectively during the Daily Scrums. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate the Daily Scrum to help the Developers stay focused, ensuring the event meets its purpose of inspecting progress toward the Sprint Goal. The Scrum Master ensures that the event takes place and is kept within the 15-minute time-box. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Facilitate the Daily Scrum to ensure it is focused and productive.
explanation1: Correct: The Scrum Master can help guide the Daily Scrum to keep it on track and productive.
answer2: Allow the Developers to conduct the Daily Scrum independently without any structure.
explanation2: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum needs structure to ensure it meets its objectives.
answer3: Cancel the Daily Scrums temporarily until the team is more organized.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is crucial for daily inspection and adaptation and should not be canceled.
answer4: Extend the timebox of the Daily Scrum to allow more discussion.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is strictly time-boxed to 15 minutes.

title: During Sprint Planning, the Developers identify that they may not have enough capacity to meet the Sprint Goal due to an upcoming holiday. What should they do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Developers must adjust the Sprint Goal and the planned work based on their realistic capacity, ensuring a feasible commitment. The Developers are solely responsible for creating a plan for the Sprint, the Sprint Backlog. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Adjust the Sprint Goal to match their available capacity.
explanation1: Correct: The Developers should plan realistically based on available capacity.
answer2: Ignore the holiday and proceed as planned.
explanation2: Incorrect: Capacity planning should account for known unavailability.
answer3: Add more work to compensate later in the Sprint.
explanation3: Incorrect: Overloading the Sprint Backlog is not a sustainable approach.
answer4: Ask the Scrum Master to extend the Sprint duration.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprints have fixed durations and cannot be extended.

title: During the Daily Scrum, the Developers realize they are not making sufficient progress toward the Sprint Goal. What should they do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Daily Scrum allows the Developers to inspect progress and adapt their plans, ensuring they remain focused on achieving the Sprint Goal. The Developers plan their work for the next 24 hours and inspect the progress toward the Sprint Goal. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Continue with the current plan and hope to catch up later.
explanation1: Incorrect: The team should inspect and adapt their plan to improve their chances of achieving the Sprint Goal.
answer2: Discuss the issues during the Daily Scrum and adjust the plan as needed.
explanation2: Correct: The Daily Scrum is the right place to inspect progress and adapt plans to meet the Sprint Goal.
answer3: Ask the Scrum Master to solve the issues for them.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates but does not directly solve issues for the team.
answer4: Wait until the Sprint Retrospective to address the issues.
explanation4: Incorrect: Issues impacting progress should be addressed immediately, not delayed until the Retrospective.

title: During the Sprint Retrospective, the team identifies that communication issues are affecting their collaboration. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions during the Retrospective to help the team identify specific actions to improve communication, enhancing collaboration and team performance. The Scrum Master ensures that the Scrum Team understands the importance of inspecting and adapting. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ignore the issue and let the team resolve it independently.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should facilitate improvements in team communication, not ignore issues.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion to identify specific communication improvements and implement them.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should help the team identify specific actions to improve communication.
answer3: Report the communication issues to management for resolution.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should handle team dynamics within the Scrum Team, not escalate to management.
answer4: Change the Daily Scrum format to address communication problems.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum’s purpose is not to address communication issues directly.

title: During the Sprint Review, stakeholders suggest changes that would impact the current Sprint Goal. What should the Scrum Team do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Team should discuss the stakeholder feedback and update the Product Backlog, ensuring that future Sprints reflect the needed changes without disrupting the current Sprint. The purpose of the Sprint Review is to inspect the outcome of the Sprint and determine future adaptations. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Immediately change the Sprint Goal to accommodate stakeholder feedback.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal is fixed once the Sprint begins and should not be changed mid-Sprint.
answer2: Discuss the feedback and update the Product Backlog for future Sprints.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Team should use the feedback to adapt future work, not change the current Sprint Goal.
answer3: Ignore the feedback as it is too late to make changes.
explanation3: Incorrect: Feedback is valuable and should be considered for future work.
answer4: End the Sprint early to start a new one with the updated goal.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprints should run their full duration unless the Sprint Goal is no longer relevant.

title: During the Sprint, the Developers find that they are unable to complete all the work they initially planned. What should they do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Developers should work with the Product Owner to adjust the Sprint Backlog, ensuring that the Sprint remains focused on achieving the Sprint Goal within the timebox. The Developers can adjust their plan each day during the Sprint, and adjust the Sprint Backlog as needed. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Ask the Scrum Master to adjust the Sprint Goal.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal remains fixed once the Sprint starts; adjustments should focus on the Sprint Backlog, not the goal.
answer2: Work with the Product Owner to adjust the Sprint Backlog as needed.
explanation2: Correct: The team should collaborate with the Product Owner to adjust the Sprint Backlog based on current progress.
answer3: Extend the Sprint duration to finish the remaining work.
explanation3: Incorrect: Sprints are time-boxed and should not be extended.
answer4: Cancel the Sprint and start over with a new plan.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprints should not be canceled unless the Sprint Goal becomes obsolete.

title: Which practice helps ensure the team consistently improves its working process during the Sprint Retrospective? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: Facilitating discussions during the Retrospective helps the team identify and agree on actionable improvements, enhancing their working process. The purpose of the Sprint Retrospective is to plan ways to increase quality and effectiveness. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Assigning improvement tasks to specific team members immediately after each Retrospective.
explanation1: Incorrect: Assigning tasks undermines the team’s collective responsibility for improvement.
answer2: Facilitating a discussion where the team identifies key improvements and agrees on actionable steps.
explanation2: Correct: Collaborative discussions ensure the team takes ownership of their improvement actions.
answer3: Having the Scrum Master decide on the improvements and assign them to the team.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Master facilitates, but improvements should be identified and owned by the team.
answer4: Skipping Retrospectives if the team feels satisfied with their current process.
explanation4: Incorrect: Retrospectives are essential for ongoing improvement, regardless of current satisfaction levels.

title: Which action should the Scrum Master take if the Developers do not meet the Sprint Goal? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: If the Sprint Goal is not met, the Scrum Master facilitates a discussion in the Sprint Retrospective to identify areas of improvement and help the team adapt. The Scrum Master ensures that the event takes place and that attendants understand its purpose. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Punish the team for not achieving the goal.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master does not punish; they coach the team toward continuous improvement.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion during the Sprint Retrospective on what went wrong.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Retrospective is the place to reflect on challenges and adjust for future Sprints.
answer3: Report the failure to stakeholders and management.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Scrum Team handles their own improvements internally without blame.
answer4: Extend the Sprint to allow more time to complete the goal.
explanation4: Incorrect: Sprints are time-boxed and should not be extended.

title: What is the primary goal of conducting Sprint Reviews with stakeholders? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Review aims to inspect the Increment, gather stakeholder feedback, and adapt the Product Backlog to better meet the product’s needs. The Sprint Review is a working session and the Scrum Team should avoid limiting it to a presentation. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: To evaluate individual team member performance based on their contributions.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Review is not an evaluation of individual performance but a collaborative discussion on the Increment.
answer2: To inspect the Increment, gather feedback, and adapt the Product Backlog accordingly.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Review helps align the product with stakeholder needs and guides future work.
answer3: To finalize the work done during the Sprint and close it out formally.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Sprint Review is a working session for feedback, not a formal closure event.
answer4: To set new priorities for the next Sprint without involving the Product Owner.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Product Owner plays a key role in setting priorities and updating the Product Backlog based on feedback.

title: What is the main function of the Sprint Goal in Scrum? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Sprint Goal provides a common objective that guides the team’s work during the Sprint, helping them stay focused and aligned. The Sprint Goal is the single objective for the Sprint. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: To assign specific tasks to team members.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal does not assign tasks; it provides focus and direction for the Sprint.
answer2: To provide a single objective for the team to achieve during the Sprint.
explanation2: Correct: The Sprint Goal offers the team a common objective and focus for the Sprint.
answer3: To measure the performance of individual Developers.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal is about team progress, not individual performance.
answer4: To define the exact amount of work that must be completed in the Sprint.
explanation4: Incorrect: The Sprint Goal guides the work but does not dictate the exact scope.

title: The Scrum Team notices that stakeholders are not actively engaging during the Sprint Review. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions with stakeholders to improve their engagement during Sprint Reviews, ensuring that their feedback is incorporated into the team's work. The Scrum Master ensures that Scrum events take place and are positive, productive, and kept within the timebox. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Report the issue to management to get stakeholders involved.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Scrum Master should address the issue directly with the stakeholders and the team, not escalate to management.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion with the stakeholders to understand their needs and improve engagement.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should engage stakeholders in discussions to ensure their feedback and needs are met.
answer3: Cancel future Sprint Reviews until stakeholders commit to attending.
explanation3: Incorrect: Sprint Reviews are essential for inspecting and adapting; they should not be canceled.
answer4: Ignore the issue and focus on team activities only.
explanation4: Incorrect: Stakeholder feedback is crucial for the Scrum Team to adapt and improve.

title: The Developers have noticed that the Daily Scrum is becoming unproductive. What is the best approach for the Scrum Master? (Choose the best answer)
feedback: The Scrum Master should facilitate discussions on improving the Daily Scrum to ensure it remains valuable. The Scrum Master ensures that the event takes place and is kept within the timebox. (Scrum Guide 2020)
answer1: Cancel the Daily Scrum until the team feels it’s needed again.
explanation1: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is essential and should not be skipped.
answer2: Facilitate a discussion to find ways to improve the Daily Scrum.
explanation2: Correct: The Scrum Master should help the team make the Daily Scrum more effective and valuable.
answer3: Assign a team member to lead the Daily Scrum.
explanation3: Incorrect: The Daily Scrum is a self-organized event led by the Developers.
answer4: Turn the Daily Scrum into a longer meeting to cover more topics.
explanation4: Incorrect: Extending the Daily Scrum can reduce its focus and efficiency.

title: A Scrum Team is struggling to incorporate stakeholder feedback into their Product Backlog efficiently. What should the Scrum Master do? (Choose the best answer)
